labels.definition: Fast-paced action gameplay with real-time combat, shooting, brawling, athletic challenge, or competitive shooters.
Adventure gameplay focused on exploration, story journeys, investigation, or point-and-click adventure.
Casual, accessible, pick-up-and-play gameplay with light challenge or short sessions.
Simulation of systems, vehicles, life, jobs, farming, cities, or realistic processes.
Strategic planning, tactics, resource decisions, wargames, or turn-based/real-time strategy.
Role-playing with character progression, classes, quests, party building, or stats-driven builds.
Sports competition such as football, basketball, racing athletics, or sports management.
Racing or driving competition with vehicles on tracks, streets, or courses.
Massively multiplayer online worlds or persistent shared multiplayer communities.
Gunplay or projectile shooting combat as a core mechanic.
First-person shooter gameplay.
Jumping and platforming traversal challenges.
Puzzle solving, logic challenges, or riddle-based progression.
Exploring spaces, discovering locations, secrets, or open areas.
Large contiguous open world to freely traverse.
Survival systems such as hunger, crafting to stay alive, or harsh resource scarcity.
Horror atmosphere, fear, monsters, or scary survival tension.
Stealth, sneaking, avoidance, or undetected infiltration gameplay.
Versus fighting game combat, martial arts duels, or arena fighters.
Roguelike runs with procedural levels, permadeath, and run-based progression.
Roguelite with run-based structure plus lasting meta-progression between runs.
Interconnected map with ability-gated backtracking exploration.

Turn-based battles where players and enemies act in turns.
Turn-based strategic or tactical map play.
Real-time strategy with base building, armies, or simultaneous command.
Tower defense: place defenses to stop waves of enemies.
Card game, deckbuilding, or card battler mechanics.
Management of resources, businesses, colonies, or complex systems.
Building, construction, base-building, or creative construction.
Crafting items from materials and recipes.
Sandbox freedom with player-driven goals and open-ended tools.
Visual novel or heavily narrative choice-driven story presentation.
Point-and-click adventure interaction style.
Narrative walking simulator focused on atmosphere and exploration over combat.
Immersive sim with systemic tools, stealth/combat choices, and emergent solutions.
Hack-and-slash combat cutting through groups of enemies.
Dense projectile patterns and bullet-hell shmup challenge.
Rhythm or music-timed gameplay.
Idle, incremental, or clicker progression gameplay.
Auto-battler or autobattler team positioning with automatic combat.
MOBA lane-based team combat with heroes.
Battle royale last-player-standing shrinking arena gameplay.
Dungeon crawling through labyrinths, loot, and encounters.
Farming simulation growing crops and tending a farm.
Life simulation of daily living, relationships, or lifestyle routines.
Grand strategy across nations, empires, diplomacy, and long-term campaigns.
Parkour or freerunning traversal movement.
Combat using vehicles, mechs, tanks, or ships.
Flight simulation or aerial combat/flying gameplay.
Digital board game or tabletop-style rules adaptation.
Party game designed for group play and light multiplayer fun.
Detective investigation, clues, and mystery solving.
Branching narrative where player choices meaningfully change outcomes.
Deep character creation or appearance/loadout customization.
Procedurally generated levels, worlds, or content.
Physics-driven puzzles, interactions, or simulation.
Score-chasing, time attack, or high-score arcade challenge.
First-person camera perspective.
Third-person camera perspective.
Top-down or overhead camera view.
Side-scrolling 2D presentation.
Two-dimensional visuals or gameplay plane.
Three-dimensional environments and visuals.
Text-based interface or prose-driven interaction.
Virtual reality support or VR-native design.
Fantasy setting with magic, mythical creatures, or medieval fantasy worlds.
Science fiction, futuristic technology, space, or sci-fi worlds.
Horror themes, cosmic dread, or terrifying subject matter.
Historical settings or real-world historical periods.
Post-apocalyptic or end-of-world aftermath setting.
War, military conflict, or large-scale armed struggle.
Crime, heists, assassins, or underworld themes.
Nature, wilderness, animals, or outdoor environmental focus.
Anime-inspired art, style, or Japanese animation aesthetics.
Romance relationships as a major theme.
Strong atmosphere, mood, and immersive ambience.
Story-rich narrative focus with characters and plot emphasis.
Comedy, humor, satire, or intentionally funny tone.
Dark, bleak, grim, or mature sombre tone.
Cute, wholesome, cozy, or adorable presentation.
Relaxing, calm, low-stress play experience.
High difficulty, punishing challenge, or hardcore demand.
Emotional storytelling intended to move the player.
Retro or old-school stylistic homage.
Colorful, vibrant, stylized visual presentation.
Realistic visuals or simulation of real-world detail.
Single-player campaign or solo play focus.
Multiplayer play with other players.
